subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class persisted cron hook lifecycle that can run user-configured shell/webhook/agent/system actions around scheduled jobs, or should these use cases stay on command cron plus plugin hook/API extensions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API controls unattended command/network execution, public cron config/protocol shape, and overlap with command cron and plugin hooks, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle contract
options.body: Define scoped pre/post/onError semantics with explicit operator authority, timeouts, output caps, redaction, audit logs, and failure/skip behavior before implementation.

options.title: Extend plugin hooks first
options.body: Add a fail-capable or gate-capable cron plugin seam so optional hook logic can live outside core while cron remains the scheduler source of truth.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Treat command cron, failure alerts, webhooks, and observe-only plugin hooks as the supported answer and narrow or close the remaining request to documentation gaps.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Define scoped pre/post/onError semantics with explicit operator authority, timeouts, output caps, redaction, audit logs, and failure/skip behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the listed project maintainer and already provided the most specific maintainer-facing routing on this issue.
